title: arXiv physics — notable recent papers, Friday 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ranking, and citation/independent-attention evidence is limited because these papers are only a few days old.

sections.title: Correlations and fluctuations of flow with event shape engineering in Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC
sections.abstract: The ALICE Collaboration measures correlations and fluctuations of flow harmonics in Pb–Pb and Xe–Xe collisions, using event-shape engineering to separate how initial geometry affects the resulting flow.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a strong v2–v3 anticorrelation and positive v2–v4 correlation, and directly resolve linear and nonlinear v4 contributions versus q2 for the first time in Pb–Pb and Xe–Xe.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Run-2 Pb–Pb (5.02 TeV) and Xe–Xe (5.44 TeV) data from 2015–2018, analyzed with event-shape engineering.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports relative systematic uncertainty for v4 of roughly 3–10%; the nonlinear-coupling coefficient also retains some q2 dependence in the most central collisions.
sections.ranking_evidence: ALICE provides a public figure set for this analysis and the paper is submitted to Physics Letters B; it reports direct flow-harmonic measurements in two collision systems and event-shape-resolved components of v4.

sections.title: The obscured nucleus of NGC3256 S. I. Anisotropic AGN near-IR radiation field traced by CO v=1-0 with JWST/NIRSpec
sections.abstract: JWST/NIRSpec CO emission from the outflow base in NGC 3256 S, interpreted with radiative-transfer models, indicates that its obscured active nucleus illuminates the outflow anisotropically.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a 4.7-μm radiation field at the outflow base about 2–4 times stronger than along our line of sight and, under a collimated-beam interpretation, a 15–20° half-opening angle and a roughly 15 ± 5 pc collimating structure.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST/NIRSpec integral-field spectroscopy and non-LTE Monte Carlo radiative-transfer fits to CO v=1–0 emission in 13 apertures.
sections.unique_caveat: The opening angle and collimator size depend on the assumed geometry and radiative-transfer model; the authors note CO-ice absorption likely contributes to underpredicted P(1)/P(2) line fluxes.
sections.ranking_evidence: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics with DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/202662221; it combines spatially resolved JWST spectroscopy with explicit radiative-transfer modeling to infer the obscured source geometry.
sections.journal_reference: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics

sections.title: Sudden disappearance of a bright exciton in solid helium
sections.abstract: The authors show that electron–hole exchange can make a prominent solid-helium exciton peak vanish for selected momentum-transfer directions near Bragg points.
sections.claimed_result: Their response analysis predicts that near a Bragg point an arbitrarily small change in momentum-transfer direction can switch a strong excitonic peak off; they discuss pressure dependence and conditions for similar effects in other materials.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; ab initio GW quasiparticle bands plus a Bethe–Salpeter electron–hole response calculation for solid-helium loss spectra, compared with previously reported experimental evidence.
sections.unique_caveat: This paper’s central result is an interpretation and prediction, not a new measurement; extension to other materials remains conditional on strong isolated excitonic peaks and significant local-field effects.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work was accepted by Physical Review B on 2 November 2026 (DOI 10.1103/z9ks-9kyk) and connects a sharply testable optical-spectra prediction to electron–hole exchange and crystal local-field effects.
sections.journal_reference: Accepted by Physical Review B on 2 November 2026

sections.title: Reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 under the Goldilocks Prior
sections.abstract: The authors reanalyze two binary-neutron-star gravitational-wave events with an equation-of-state-informed prior and find that source tidal-deformability posteriors can shift substantially relative to uniform-prior analyses.
sections.claimed_result: For GW170817, the most probable tidal deformability of the lighter star rises from about 215 to 443 under the Goldilocks rather than uniform prior; for GW190425, allowed deformabilities contract, while its equation-of-state constraints remain more prior-sensitive.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Bayesian reanalysis of GW170817 and GW190425 gravitational-wave data with spectral and Gaussian-process equation-of-state ensembles.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is explicitly prior-dependent: the two prior treatments give differing GW190425 equation-of-state constraints, while the joint constraints are largely dominated by GW170817.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper is cross-listed across gravitation and high-energy astrophysics and points to a public LIGO Document Control Center companion (P2600110-v3); it quantifies how prior choice changes inferred neutron-star properties.
sections.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, and with End Matter, https://dcc.ligo.org/P2600110-v3

sections.title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
sections.abstract: Coupled-cluster emulators are used to connect quadrupole geometry in ultrarelativistic oxygen and neon collisions to the low-energy constants of chiral nuclear interactions.
sections.claimed_result: At next-to-next-to-leading order, the authors find linear, additive sensitivity of quadrupole eccentricity to all 16 chiral-interaction constants; 20Ne collisions are especially sensitive to the two-nucleon spin–orbit interaction.
sections.evidence_type: computational; subspace-projected coupled-cluster emulators and global sensitivity analysis, motivated by measured LHC 16O+16O and 20Ne+20Ne collective flow.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a sensitivity map at a specified order in the chiral expansion, not a new extraction of the force parameters from collision data; conclusions depend on the interaction and emulator framework.
sections.ranking_evidence: It is cross-listed across nuclear theory, phenomenology, and experiment and makes a concrete bridge between LHC light-ion flow observables and parameters of low-energy nuclear forces.

sections.title: Analytic Marginalization Over Calibration Uncertainties in Gravitational Wave Inference and Application to Black Hole Ringdown
sections.abstract: The authors extend spline-based calibration-uncertainty marginalization to the time domain and apply it to black-hole ringdown analyses.
sections.claimed_result: After calibration marginalization, the authors retain evidence for two modes in GW250114; for GW250207, the remnant mass and spin agree with full-signal estimates, but no second mode is supported.
sections.evidence_type: computational; analytic time-domain inference with basis splines, applied to LIGO ringdown data for GW250114 and GW250207.
sections.unique_caveat: The lack of evidence for a second GW250207 mode means the analysis does not tightly constrain deviations from general relativity during that ringdown.
sections.ranking_evidence: The method is cross-listed in gravitation and astrophysical instrumentation and is demonstrated on two recent high-signal-to-noise ringdowns, making the calibration treatment directly relevant to strong-field inference.

sections.title: Latest $ν$s from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
sections.abstract: The authors combine JWST high-redshift-galaxy UV luminosity functions with Planck CMB data to constrain possible neutrino self-interactions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 95% upper limits on log10(G_eff/MeV⁻²) of about −2.75 for one interacting neutrino flavor and −3.41 when all three flavors interact, tighter than their Planck-only bounds.
sections.evidence_type: observational; cosmological parameter-constraint analysis using JWST UV luminosity functions and Planck CMB data.
sections.unique_caveat: These are conditional upper limits, not evidence of a detection; the inferred bound depends on the interacting-flavor scenario and the modeling that maps early-galaxy abundances to small-scale matter power.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper bridges cosmology and particle phenomenology and applies JWST’s high-redshift UV-luminosity data jointly with CMB constraints to a beyond-Standard-Model interaction parameter.

sections.title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors construct a decoder for a symmetry-enriched toric-code memory and prove exponentially decreasing logical error with system size under the paper’s noise model for a sufficient symmetry-size bound.
sections.claimed_result: For a honeycomb toric code coupled to Sp(N) rotors, the authors show exponentially decreasing logical error for N ≥ 40 at any bond error probability in [0,1] under incoherent electric noise; they also extend the construction to other symmetries.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; minimum-weight decoder and logical-error analysis for a symmetry-enriched toric-code model.
sections.unique_caveat: N ≥ 40 is a conservative sufficient condition for the specified model and noise channel, not an experimentally demonstrated hardware threshold or an optimized minimum.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper is cross-listed between quantum physics and strongly correlated matter and gives an explicit decoder construction with a quantified sufficient bound, rather than only proposing a qualitative protection mechanism.
